## File: /website/articles/case-studies.html

### Body Text:
- A data-driven breakdown of optimizing delivery mechanics from 166 WPM to 123 WPM by leveraging personal storytelling.
- Specialist in Speech Biomechanics. Helping leaders measure and optimize spoken delivery.
- Click to load the free verision of the Mic-Check App. See your own speech metrics and practice improving how you speak.
- The browser app requires microphone permissions to analyze your delivery.
- Narmada is a senior auditor evaluating food safety and dysphagia standards across hospitality and aged-care facilities. When she was tapped to deliver her first major presentation at the Hospitality in Healthcare (HIH) Conference, the pressure triggered immediate Skill Inhibition.
- During her initial THPS Speech Assessment, the baseline data revealed exactly how the pressure was manifesting:
- To prepare for the HIH Conference, we transitioned into the 1-on-1 THPS Performance Plan. To reduce her 12.6-second Runtime, Narmada needed to build muscle memory around deliberate, structural pauses.
- We completely restructured her presentation content. Instead of quoting regulatory guidelines, we drafted a deeply Visual and Personal narrative. We anchored her speech to a vivid, high-stakes scenario: "Imagine it is 12:05 pm in an aged-care home... One resident requires a texture-modified meal. Another has a documented milk allergy."
- By Session 4, the transformation in her Mic-Check dashboard was profound. By leaning into personal storytelling, her content metrics shifted to 59% Personal and 18% Visual. Because she felt emotionally connected to the material, her pace naturally dropped to an authoritative 123 WPM, and her Runtime normalized to 5.5 seconds.
- She walked into the HIH Conference not just surviving the presentation, but commanding the room with a final grading of 96.0 / 100.
- While the Mic-Check App measured Narmada's pacing and pauses, the underlying driver of her success was a massive reduction in cognitive load. Here is how her working memory shifted from Red-Zone overload to effortless execution.
- The Bottleneck: Attempting to manually memorize regulatory scripts pushed Narmada's working memory past 110% capacity, triggering the SAM Axis and shutting down her pacing control.
- The Breakthrough: By relying on familiar visual stories and Repeat/Count structures, her speech execution dropped to an 8% cognitive load, freeing her brain to command the room dynamically.
- Visualized progression based on client self-reporting mapped to the Fitts & Posner motor-learning model. Not a physical biometric measurement.
- Unlike basic word-counting scripts, our proprietary THPS.analyzeSpeech engine evaluates spoken audio across multiple biomechanical dimensions in real time:
- We calculate syllable counts per word token and map gaps against expected syllable unit lengths. A pause is classified as a structural breath or cadence break only when silence exceeds 700ms to 750ms.
- Continuous speech runs between structural pauses are classified into absolute cadence tiers:
                                &gt;5.0 SPS (Too Fast), 
                                3.8–4.2 SPS (Optimal Command Zone), and 
                                &lt;3.0 SPS (Drag Zone).
- Spoken energy is continuously grouped using biological decibel thresholds (±3dB and ±9dB relative to the speaker’s average spoken word intensity) to track dynamic contrast vs. monotone strain on a real-time Voice Graph.
- Transcripts are evaluated against normalized dictionaries (including 10k Common Words and Visual Imagery corpora) to calculate grade level, narrative pronoun density, and visual clarity without relying on subjective opinions.
- Get your own baseline analytics and discover the exact metrics holding back your communication.

## File: /website/articles/glossary.html

### Body Text:
- Public speaking improves when you replace subjective feedback with objective data. Browse our standardized definitions for speech delivery metrics, diagnostic tests, and coaching frameworks.
- THPS stands for Tom Hendrick Public Speaking, and is the overarching brand and legal entity (Thomas Geoffrey Hendrick) headquartered at Suite 110, 147 Pirie Street, Adelaide and providing online public speaking assessment and coaching globally.
- A free, 1-hour, 5-step data-driven diagnostic session used to measure presentation anxiety, unscripted fluency, and vocal inhibition.
- A premium 4-week, 1-on-1 intensive coaching program ($990 AUD) designed to move executives from cognitive strain to effortless delivery.
- An app to turn public speaking practice into measurable data that provides insights on how to improve your speaking skills. The Mic-Check App is akin to a golf launch monitor for public speaking, as it is a web browser-based educational application able to process live and recorded audio data into natural language displayed on a dashboard of insightful speaking metrics.
- The premium subscription tier ($9.90 AUD/month) for the full Mic-Check app that unlocks historical tracking, speaking courses and games, and other advanced features.
- A free, weekly online group practice class focusing on unscripted speaking and measured accountability.
- A gamified aggregate score out of 10 in the Mic-Check App, where hitting all 9 metric targets awards a perfect 10/10.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App, WPM stands for Words Per Minute and is about how many words the speaker says per minute on average (including time speaking and time pausing). There is an upper limit on how many words audiences can process effectively in a minute. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 100 to 150 WPM.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App, SPS stands for Syllables Per Second and is about how many syllables the speaker said in an average second (excluding any time pausing). There is an upper limit on how many syllables audiences can process effectively in a second before words sound like they are incoherent mumbles. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 3.5 to 4.5 syllables per second.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App, Pause % is the amount of time the speaker paused compared to their active speaking time. Too much Pause % suggests hesitation, not enough Pause % suggests rushing. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 15 to 35% Pause %.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about how long a speaker talks on average until they take a Noticeable Pause (a pause longer than 700 milliseconds). Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 3 to 6 seconds of runtime until they take a Noticeable Pause.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about pauses with a duration longer than 700 milliseconds. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers include pauses between 700ms to 2 seconds on average every 3 to 6 seconds of Runtime.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about how much of your content describes a specific person’s thoughts and actions (e.g., “I think”, “he said”, “she won”, etc.). A lack of personal content is at risk of being unengaging or vague. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 10 to 30% Intangible content.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about how much of your content describes words people are capable of visualising (e.g., colours, sizes, locations, objects, etc.). A lack of Visual content is at risk of being unengaging or vague. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 10 to 30% Intangible content.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about how much of your content describes non-Personal and non-Visual words (e.g., general concepts, mere grammar, filler words). Too much intangible content is at risk of being overly technical, dry or unmemorable. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 10 to 30% Intangible content.
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about the complexity of the speaker’s average sentence, in terms of word length and syllable count. Comp-Grade compares the speaker’s sentence complexity against reading comprehension indexes like Flesch Kinkaid, Fog, Smog, or Coleman-Liau. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 5th to 10th grade reading levels (plain english).
- A metric measured on the Mic-Check App about how many words matched a database of the 10,000 most commonly used English words by non-native English speakers. Too much Simple % is at risk of not introducing technically correct concepts or novel engaging words. Too little Simple % is at risk of being overly technical, inaccessible language. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 80 to 90% Simple %.
- The foundational premise of THPS coaching. Skill Inhibition is the concept of how much perceived pressure causes one’s speaking skills to decline. Skill Inhibition in speaking is akin to a professional golfer hitting a bad shot under pressure.
- A diagnostic component of the Speech Assessment evaluating physiological stress and fight-or-flight responses.
- A psychological assessment tool used to measure a speaker's capacity for visual thinking.
- A diagnostic exercise used to measure the physical or mental barriers restricting a speaker's natural voice.
- An assessment exercise testing unscripted fluency by having the client speak prompted by visual cues.
- An assessment exercise designed to measure a speaker's cognitive load and delivery mechanics while adhering to specific constraints.
- Stop guessing about your pacing, pauses, and clarity. Book your free 1-hour assessment to map your exact baseline data.

## File: /website/articles/sams-test.html

### Body Text:
- Discover exactly when and why your brain triggers presentation anxiety.
- This survey takes 2 minutes and will help you map your specific psychological pressure profile. Your data will be saved to your dashboard.
- Results safely stored to your CRM.
- Read below to learn how pressure affects your performance
- Public speaking is not just a psychological event; it is a biomechanical and neurological one. To fully understand why your voice shakes, why you ramble, or why you go completely blank under pressure, we must look at the biological systems in your brain.
- This is your body's unconscious threat detection network. Because your primitive brain (specifically the amygdala and hypothalamus) does not conceptually understand "public speaking," it interprets the physical environment—standing alone, blinded by lights, facing a social majority—as an immediate survival threat (being surrounded by predators).
- Your brain divides its control between conscious actions (the voluntary system) and automatic, life-sustaining functions (the involuntary system). A speaker's success under pressure is dictated entirely by how well they manage the division of labor between these two.
- When the SAM Axis perceives a severe threat, your brain initiates a ruthless energy trade-off. Think of a city's power grid during a severe winter storm. When total collapse is imminent, the city intentionally cuts power to the suburbs (the language and reasoning centers of the cerebral cortex) to ensure the hospitals and water pumps (the primitive survival centers) have 100% of the remaining electricity.
- Once a speaker breaches this "Red Zone," their language and reasoning faculties are biologically forced offline. You cannot logic your way out of the Red Zone. A Red-Zoned speaker is physically incapable of generative language. This is exactly why you "blank out."
- The untrained speaker attempts to run their entire presentation through conscious, manual effort—trying to control exact word choice, pacing, and body language simultaneously. This severely overloads working memory.
- Through deliberate, constraint-based practice (like the THPS Vocal Mechanics Method), we train your brain to execute familiar routines under pressure, signaling "predictive success" to your amygdala. When the primitive brain feels safe, it stops the cortisol flow, preventing the hijack and keeping your language centers fully powered.
- The Sympathetic Adreno-medullary System (SAM Axis) is the biological pathway that controls your fight-or-flight response. In public speaking, it is responsible for the physical symptoms of nervousness, such as a racing heart, shallow breathing, and mental blanking when facing an audience.
- Going blank is caused by cognitive overload pushing your brain into the "Red Zone." Your amygdala detects a threat and pulls blood and electrical priority away from your prefrontal cortex (the part of your brain that generates language), leaving you temporarily unable to access your vocabulary or structure.
- You cannot logic your way out of biological nerves. The best way to eliminate presentation anxiety is to build automated muscle memory (like the THPS Repeat and Count framework). When your speaking structure becomes autonomous, your brain registers safety, and the nervous system remains calm under pressure.

## File: /website/articles/vviq-test.html

### Body Text:
- Discover your cognitive imagery profile and stop going blank under pressure.
- This survey shows how you prefer to think and speak without a script. Some people ‘see’ images in their mind, some people see nothing but think in rules & categories. Keep your eyes open and try to ‘see’ what is described.
- Results safely stored to your CRM.
- Read below to learn how your imagery profile affects your speaking
- The purpose of this page is to gauge whether the user/speaker prefers to think in images when they think and speak, or in rules/concepts. We plot where they land on the cognitive imagery spectrum.
- A major pitfall speakers fall into is they don't know if they have Aphantasia, Hypophantasia, Phantasia, or Hyperphantasia. Consequently, when it comes to thinking and speaking without a script, they try to think and speak against the grain of how their brain fluently operates.
- Example: A hyperphantasia person can effortlessly (and involuntarily) find words by associating them with images and memories. They say a word like "house" and lots of vivid details quickly come to mind. However, if that speaker gets nervous during preparation about forgetting their content, they might force themselves to memorize rigid dot points. Because non-visual dot points run completely against the grain of their hyperphantasia preference, they are highly likely to go blank when prompted by that cue under pressure.
- According to current clinical statistics on population distributions, approximately 0.9% of the population has Aphantasia, 3.3% have Hypophantasia, 89.7% have typical imagery ability (Phantasia), and 6.1% possess Hyperphantasia.
- An inability to see images in your mind. People with Aphantasia are often effortlessly able to use multiple speaking skills when they speak, but struggle to improvise, or give vivid, personal, or specific examples.
- Aphantasia speakers tend to improve rules-based (non-image-based) skills faster than the other speaker types. When no structure or process comes to mind they are at risk of going blank, because they have no way to generate images in their mind.
- Hypophantasia means it takes effort to see images in your mind and those images might be disobedient and not vivid (Tom Hendrick has Hypophantasia, leaning toward Aphantasia).
- Hypophantasia speakers are often good at using multiple speaking skills when they speak, but find it hard (but not impossible) to give vivid, personal, and specific examples when speaking. Hypophantasia speakers tend to improve these image-based skills faster than Aphantasia speakers.
- The average person can recall or see images in their mind easily when speaking. Although they may not initially excel at juggling multiple speaking skills at once, or giving vivid, personal, and specific examples—they tend to learn and improve all of these skills the fastest.
- Effortlessly seeing images in one’s mind. A Hyperphantasia speaker can quickly conjure an image in their mind from word or image prompts—and does so effortlessly to the point multiple images or a ‘mental movie’ plays in their head involuntarily.
- Hyperphantasia speakers tend to excel the most at giving vivid, personal, and specific examples, but can struggle the most with structuring a speech or using multiple speaking skills at the same time. When no image comes to mind they are at risk of going blank unless they learn non-image-based skills (like the Repeat & Count framework).
- The VVIQ is a psychological assessment tool used to measure a speaker's capacity for visual thinking, placing them on a spectrum from Aphantasia (no mental imagery) to Hyperphantasia (extremely vivid mental imagery).
- An inability to see images in your mind. Aphantasia speakers tend to improve rules-based (non-image-based) skills faster than the other speaker types. When no structure or process comes to mind they are at risk of going blank, because they have no way to generate images in their mind.
- You should not memorize a script. Instead, you should prompt yourself using methods that match your VVIQ profile. Hyperphantasic speakers should use visual cues, while Aphantasic speakers should rely on structural frameworks like the Repeat and Count method.

## File: /website/members/privacy.html

### Body Text:
- Effective Date: October 23, 2026
- As the best online public speaking coach, Tom Hendrick Public Speaking processes your vocal performance analytics securely. We never sell your personal information. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests that protecting client confidentiality is essential for building the trust required to eliminate presentation anxiety.
- The Mic-Check App requires microphone access to measure speaking metrics like WPM and Pause %, but audio processing happens securely on your device. Unless you actively link your CRM account for a THPS Performance Plan, voice recordings are not transmitted to our servers.
- Yes. All THPS Speech Assessment and coaching sessions are strictly confidential. We do not share your corporate strategies or personal stories. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests a secure environment is critical to safely diagnosing and reversing Skill Inhibition under pressure.
- This Privacy Policy explains how Tom Hendrick Public Speaking ("Provider", "we", "us", "our") collects, uses, and protects your personal data when you visit tomhendrick.com, use the Mic-Check App, or participate in our coaching services.
- We collect information that you voluntarily provide to us when you register on the Member Portal, express an interest in obtaining information about us or our products, or otherwise contact us. This may include:
- The free version of the Mic-Check App processes your audio and text inputs locally within your web browser to generate your real-time speaking metrics.
- If you upgrade to Mic-Check Pro or actively link your CRM account via the Member Portal, your performance data and historical progress charts are securely transmitted and stored on our cloud servers. This allows your coach to review your progress during your THPS Performance Plan sessions.
- We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties. We treat all information discussed during your THPS Speech Assessment and private coaching sessions as strictly confidential. We only share information with third-party vendors, service providers, and contractors who perform services for us or on our behalf (e.g., payment processing, data hosting) and require access to such information to do that work.
- We may use cookies and similar tracking technologies to access or store information. This helps us understand how users interact with the Mic-Check App and our website, allowing us to improve the user experience and ensure the platform functions correctly.
- You have the right to review, change, or terminate your account at any time. You may disconnect your coaching integration via the "CRM Link" tab in the Member Portal, which will immediately stop the transmission of your diagnostic data to your coach. Upon request to terminate your account, we will deactivate or delete your account and information from our active databases.
- If you have questions or comments about this Privacy Policy, or if you wish to exercise your data rights, please contact us directly via the contact form on our website or email us at our registered business address.

## File: /website/services/mic-check-app.html

### Body Text:
- Stop guessing how you sound. Use the dashboard below to record a brief baseline, then view your full data-driven speaking metrics and vocal performance report.
- Click to load the live speech analyzer. Speak into your microphone to measure your pacing, pauses, and vocabulary.
- The browser app requires microphone permissions to analyze your delivery.
- Our proprietary engine breaks your communication down into three measurable categories: Content, Delivery, and Simplicity. Here is how your data translates to a better performance.
- The Personal metric measures storytelling by tracking how much of your content describes a specific person’s thoughts and actions. A lack of personal content risks being unengaging or vague. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 30 to 60% Personal content.
- The Visual metric measures how much of your content relies on sensory words people can visualize, like colors, sizes, or objects. Low visual scores limit audience retention. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 20 to 50% Visual content.
- The Intangible metric measures how much of your content describes non-Personal and non-Visual words, such as general concepts or filler. Too much intangible content makes speeches dry. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 10 to 30% Intangible content.
- WPM stands for Words Per Minute and measures how many words the speaker says per minute on average. There is an upper limit on how many words audiences process effectively. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 100 to 150 WPM.
- SPS stands for Syllables Per Second and functions as our Mumble Meter. It measures syllables spoken per active second, excluding pauses. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 3.5 to 4.5 SPS before words sound like incoherent mumbles.
- Pause % is the amount of time the speaker spent completely silent compared to their active speaking time. Too little pause time indicates rushing. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 15 to 35% Pause %.
- Variance metrics track your vocal dynamics. Pause Var evaluates varied pause lengths, Voice Var counts changes in speaking volume, and Pace Var tracks alternating slow and fast sentences. High variation in these three metrics directly correlates with highly engaging and persuasive delivery.
- Runtime measures how long a speaker talks on average until they take a Noticeable Pause longer than 700 milliseconds. Extreme runtimes indicate nervous rushing. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers average a Runtime between 3.0 to 6.0 seconds.
- Comp-Grade measures the complexity of your average sentence against reading comprehension indexes like Flesch Kinkaid or Coleman-Liau. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 5.0 to 10.0 Comp-Grade, indicating accessible, plain English.
- Simple % calculates how many words match a database of the 10,000 most commonly used English words. Too little Simple % risks alienating your audience with overly technical language. Our database of measured professional speakers suggests the best speakers range between 80 to 90% Simple %.
- The Score Summary measures your Content, Delivery, and Simplicity. Metrics in the green zone get +10 points to formulate your total Grade out of 100.
- The Green Score counts how many of the 9 core metrics hit the perfect Green Zone (+10). Each green metric adds +1 to this score. Getting all 9 greens awards a +1 bonus, for a perfect 10/10.
- Your final Grade is a score out of 100. It is the sum of your 9 core metrics (max 90 points) plus your Green Score (max 10 points).
- The free demo resets after every use. Subscribe to unlock cloud history, detailed PDF reports, and advanced speaking courses.

## File: /website/services/thps-performance-plan.html

### Body Text:
- The THPS Performance Plan is a premium 4-week, 1-on-1 online coaching program ($990 AUD). The program is designed specifically to move executives from cognitive strain to effortless, autonomous speaking under pressure using live audio data and structured constraints.
- Skill Inhibition: The speaker is rushing at an unsustainable 197 WPM with massive 18.8-second Runtimes, resulting in a failing engagement score.
- Skill Acquisition: After 4 sessions, pacing optimizes to 112 WPM. The historical progress chart stabilizes at 100/100 across multiple high-pressure attempts.
- You do not have a skill acquisition problem; you have a Skill Inhibition problem. When facing a high-stakes pitch, your amygdala detects a threat, causing you to rush your words or lose your structure.
- Through deliberate, constraint-based practice like the Repeat & Count framework, we train your brain to execute familiar routines under pressure, bypassing the panic response entirely.
- What exactly happens to your working memory when you step onto a stage? Map the Fitts & Posner Reverse S-Curve and test your own cognitive capacity limits in real-time.
- Delivered globally via Zoom, the THPS Performance Plan transitions you from high mental effort to real-time self-correction. We utilize advanced storytelling constraints to drastically increase your cognitive load in practice, meaning the attention required to structure your thoughts during a real presentation drops to near zero. Your delivery becomes composed, and your WPM stabilizes flawlessly.
- In this initial stage, mental effort is high as we override your biological panic response. We introduce rigid constraint frameworks like Repeat & Count, forcing your brain to declare structure upfront before you are allowed to speak, preventing rambling and rapid pacing.
- We transition into real-time self-correction. You will learn to use familiar structural prompts (like Problem, Options, Solution) to send calming signals back to your own nervous system (Self-Regulation) while projecting absolute certainty to your audience (Co-Regulation).
- We drastically increase the cognitive load. By utilizing advanced storytelling constraints (like Say What You See), we train your brain to rapidly "zip-file" thousands of relevant thoughts from a single visual prompt, allowing you to handle hostile Q&A effortlessly without a script.
- This is the holy grail of public speaking. The attention required to structure your thoughts drops to near zero. Your delivery is composed, your pacing is flawless, and your Mic-Check App historical progress chart consistently locks in at 100/100.
- The THPS Performance Plan is delivered as 4x 1-Hour Private Sessions.
- The THPS Performance Plan is a $990 AUD investment. Because it is highly tailored to your specific biomechanical and cognitive gaps, it cannot be purchased directly. All clients must complete a baseline diagnostic first.
- Book your Free 1-Hour THPS Speech Assessment today to establish your data baseline. At the end of your assessment, Tom will review your eligibility for the 4-week program.

## File: /website/services/thps-speech-assessment.html

### Body Text:
- Nerves can strip away your speaking skills under pressure. Discover exactly why your delivery breaks down—and how to fix it—with a free 1-hour acoustic and cognitive baseline diagnostic.
- A Google Meet invitation has been securely dispatched to your email address.
- Capable professionals often know their material intimately but find preparing for presentations exhausting. Over-relying on clunky scripts takes away natural delivery, while speaking unscripted brings the fear of going off-track or blanking completely.
- The THPS Speech Assessment replaces subjective feedback with clinical, data-driven insights. Before you book a Performance Plan, we spend 1 hour (online or in-person) running you through 5 core diagnostic tests to map your unique communication gaps.
- Pinpoint exactly when and why your body triggers presentation anxiety. By measuring your neuro-hormonal response to speaking cues, we identify your specific Preparation Dysregulation gap compared to hundreds of benchmarked executives.
- Discover why memorizing clunky scripts is holding you back. We plot your cognitive imagery profile on the spectrum from Aphantasia to Hyperphantasia, revealing whether your brain relies on vivid visual concepts or rigid structural rules when speaking off-the-cuff.
- Measure the psychological blocks causing a monotone delivery under pressure. You will attempt to deliver a script using extreme vocal ranges (fast, slow, loud, quiet). This benchmarks your ability to modulate pitch and volume on command, identifying your exact Vocal Inhibition Gap.
- Benchmark your natural ability to speak vividly. Using the Mic-Check App, we capture your baseline Words Per Minute (WPM) and visual descriptor percentages when prompted solely by imagery or imagination, measuring your core fluency strengths.
- Find out exactly when your speaking fluency breaks down. We impose progressive constraints across 6 rounds of questioning to test how quickly you lose composure under complex Q&A rules and high cognitive load.
- The resulting data from your free assessment allows us to build your highly personalized 4-week Performance Plan. By integrating targeted rules, progressive constraints, and daily tracking via the Mic-Check App, we close your exact gaps so you can speak with composure under immense pressure.
- "The initial assessment revealed a massive rules-based communication gap I didn't even know I had. Measuring my WPM in real time completely changed how I approach hostile Q&A."
- Scroll up to book your free 1-hour session online or in-person at our Adelaide clinic.
